data.title: Introduce new social investment programs supporting  Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) particularly among the poor.
data.promise_blog:
During his Renewed Hope election campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu pledged to introduce new social investment programs to foster the growth of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), with a particular focus on supporting economically disadvantaged communities.

This commitment aims to stimulate Nigeria’s economy by creating job opportunities and strengthening the MSME and nano-business landscape, encouraging broader participation and sustainable growth. Recognizing the limited success of previous government efforts to develop MSMEs despite significant resource allocations, the Tinubu administration has introduced targeted programs since its inauguration. These initiatives provide funding, training, and capacity-building support to enhance MSME participation, empower entrepreneurs, and drive economic resilience across the nation.

updates.blog:
PRESIDENTIAL INTERVENTION FUND TARGETS MSMES WITH ₦200 BILLION ALLOCATION, PROGRESS UNDERWAY

The Federal Government has begin the distribution of ₦75 billion to MSMEs and another ₦75 billion distributed to the manufacturing industry under the Presidential Intervention Fund”. The Federal Government in March 2024 began disbursing the ₦50,000 Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, also known as the Trade Grants Scheme, to nano businesses nationwide. Nano businesses are enterprises that have one or two workers and less than an annual turnover of N3 million.

This intervention by the government so far is aimed at helping MSMEs find their feet and improve the economy, but more needs to be done to improve on what was done by previous governments. This promise is rated “In The Works”.
